Set up the `syskit` module (rename `example.com/syskit` in `go.mod` to your real path):

```
go.mod / go.sum
cmd/syskit/main.go
internal/platform/platform.go            SystemInfo type
internal/platform/platform_linux.go     //go:build linux   -> unix.Uname
internal/platform/platform_darwin.go    //go:build darwin  -> unix.Uname
internal/platform/platform_windows.go   //go:build windows -> windows.RtlGetNtVersionNumbers
internal/platform/platform_unsupported.go //go:build !linux && !darwin && !windows
.gitignore
```

Key points:
- Uses `golang.org/x/sys` (v0.48.0) for syscalls the stdlib doesn't expose; pure Go, no cgo, so cross-compiles cleanly.
- One build-tagged file per OS behind an identical `platform.Info() (SystemInfo, error)` API.
- Verified with go1.26: `go vet` + `go build` pass for `linux/arm64`, `darwin/amd64`, `windows/amd64`; the Linux binary runs.

Build examples:
```
go build ./cmd/syskit
GOOS=darwin  GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o syskit-macos   ./cmd/syskit
GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o syskit.exe     ./cmd/syskit
```

Note: I installed Go 1.26 to `/tmp/opencode/go` for verification only; it's not on your PATH.
